analysis.investment_thesis: A tiny copper-scrap recycler with a 0.20% ROE is not a business I'd ever own — there's no moat in recycling commodity metal, and the economics are dreadful. At 12x earnings this looks cheap only until you realize you're paying for near-zero profitability.
key_risks: ROE of 0.20% — essentially destroying capital vs. cost of equity
Commodity pass-through business with zero pricing power or moat
Micro-cap (INR 189 Cr) with negligible institutional ownership (DII 0.03%, FII 0%)
red_flags: ROE near zero is incompatible with a real business franchise
Recent incorporation (2016) + recent listing — unproven through a full copper cycle
No competitive moat in copper scrap recycling — pure tolling margins
analysis.detailed_analysis:
A 0.20% return on equity tells you everything you need to know. In my entire career I've insisted on businesses earning 15%+ on equity consistently; this one isn't even clearing a savings account rate. Copper-rod-from-scrap is a classic commodity conversion business — you buy scrap at spot, sell rod at spot minus a conversion charge, and your margin is dictated entirely by LME pricing and local competition. There is no brand, no switching cost, no network effect, no regulatory moat. The 12x P/E is meaningless when the "E" is a sliver on a fat equity base.

The 72% promoter holding is the one positive — owner mentality matters — but you cannot fix commodity economics with good intentions. A micro-cap at INR 189 Cr with virtually no institutional sponsorship, incorporated only in 2016, listed recently, operating in a cyclical metals niche — this sits well outside any reasonable circle of competence for a long-term compounder. I'd pass without a second look and wait for a wonderful business at a fair price instead.
